title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR Pelagian parallel; PLAC deny immediate-catholic tip
pass_a_gloss: GAR answers generally: if such pinpoint questions are allowed, Pelagians or Socinians could as speciously harry original corruption as this imputation doctrine is harried here—why Adam's moral corruption infected posterity rather than theirs him; why his sin must descend and other fathers' not; why his hurt Cain but Cain's not him; why the first corrupted us more than later ones; why Adam was freed and infants not; why Christ is our righteousness/sanctification but Adam not our sin/corruption. If those do not block acknowledging inborn corruption, neither should these quibbles stop perseverance in the old Catholic faith of imputation. PLAC: Is immediate imputation's faith thus ancient and catholic? That is neither proved yet nor proveable.
pass_b_english: GAR. VII. But we answer. I. Generally. If there ought to be room for such pinpoint interrogations, the doctrine of Original corruption can be no less speciously harassed by the followers of Pelagius or Socinus than this doctrine of imputation is vexed here. For it would be asked 1. Why Adam's moral corruption rather infected posterity than posterity's corruption stained Adam? 2. Why Adam's sin necessarily descended into posterity, and that of other fathers not so? 3. Why Adam's sin hurt Cain, and Cain's sin hurt Adam not at all? 4. Why the first sin rather corrupted us than Adam's following sins? 5. Why was Adam freed from that corruption ... and all infants ... not freed? 6. Why is Christ called our righteousness and sanctification, and Adam not called our sin and corruption? These and other things can be asked against the doctrine of inborn corruption, which if they do not hinder the learned man from having to acknowledge that corruption, neither ought those little questions to be an impediment to us from persevering in the ancient and Catholic faith of imputation. PLAC. Is the faith of immediate imputation thus ancient and catholic? That has neither been proved thus far, nor can it be proved.
source_text: GAR. VII. Nos vero respondemus. I. Generaliter. Si ejusmodi interrogationum punctulis locus esse debeat, non minus speciose sollicitari posse doctrinam de corruptione Originali a Pelagii aut Socini sectatoribus, quam haec de imputatione doctrina hic vexatur. Quaeretur enim 1. Cur Adami corruptio moralis posteros potius infecit, quam corruptio posterorum inquinavit Adamum? 2. Cur Adami peccatum in posteros necessario descendit, caeterorum patrum non ita descendit? 3. Cur Adami peccatum Caino nocuit, Caini peccatum Adamo minime nocuit? 4. Cur primum peccatum nos potius corrupit, quam sequentia? 5. Cur Adamus ab illa corruptione liberatus est ... infantes omnes ... non liberantur? 6. Cur Christus justitia & sanctificatio nostra dicitur, Adamus non dicitur peccatum & corruptio nostra? Haec & alia adversus doctrinam de corruptione ingenita queri possunt, quae si non obstant quominus Viri docti corruptionem illam agnoscere debeant; neque debent quaestiunculae illae impedimento nobis esse, quominus in antiqua & Catholica imputationis fide perseveremus. PLAC. Itane antiqua & catholica est imputationis immediatae fides? Id neque probatum est hactenus, neque probari potest.
